magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that dialogue must rest on truth and mutual respect for the dignity of the interlocutor is in accordance with Catholic teaching; dialogue does not require keeping silent about untruth nor an apparent agreement. Nevertheless, the expression that the other side „holds a knife behind their back” can, if not supported by concrete evidence or applied generally, unjustly attribute dishonest intentions to interlocutors and weaken the Christian spirit of dialogue.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of dialogue does not reduce it to polite socializing or compromise: participants must sincerely seek the truth, be ready to listen to it and correct themselves, and a false agreement reached through deception is not true dialogue. At the same time, the believer should present the truth with gentleness and respect, as 1 Peter 3:15 encourages, and avoid attributing dishonest methods without basis; therefore, it is possible to decisively challenge untruth while still preserving justice and openness toward the interlocutor.
concerns_en: The metaphor of the „knife behind the back” can encourage suspicion or the collective attribution of evil intent; the Catholic approach demands truthfulness, but also respect, patience, and refraining from discrediting those with whom we disagree without sufficient reasons.
From the provided excerpt, it is not possible to assess whether the concrete claims about the behavior of the other side are factually grounded.

sections.subtitle_en: Dialogue yes, but not at the price of truth
sections.screenshot_description_en: Msgr. Košić explains that Catholic dialogue must be prudent and dignified
sections.content_en:
The bishop explains his stance on dialogue with a personal comparison. If someone were to say of his father that he was a murderer or a violent man and attributed to him what he did not do, he would tell him to *stop telling untruths* because he cannot talk to him that way. In his opinion, that is a **matter of dignity** of both the interlocutor himself and the level of dialogue.

He sharply criticizes, as he says, apparent dialogue in which people *hug and take photos in front of cameras, eat, drink, and celebrate*, while the other side *holds a knife behind their back*. „Is that dialogue that should be Catholic dialogue?“, he asks.

His answer is not a rejection of dialogue. On the contrary, he emphasizes that Catholics are **absolutely for dialogue** and that everything should be done to **bring East and West closer**. Catholics must know how to restrain themselves, be *diplomats as well*, and make concessions in some places. But Catholic dialogue must be **prudent dialogue**, and one boundary remains immovable: **we must not sacrifice the truth**.

sections.subtitle: Od Župnika do Biskupa na prvoj crti: propovijedi, poezija i razgovor sa svetim Petrom
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pokazuje knjigu Biskup na prvoj crti, a gost objašnjava kako je nastala
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća na bogat pisani opus mons. Košića. Uz knjigu **„Župnik na prvoj crti“** izašao je i nastavak **„Biskup na prvoj crti“**, koji voditelj pokazuje u studiju. Biskup je napisao i **zbirku poezije**, a ima i talent za pjevanje. Voditelja zanima postoji li još koji talent za koji javnost ne zna.

Biskup najprije pojašnjava nastanak druge knjige. „Biskupa na prvoj crti“ predložili su mu suradnici nakon izlaska „Župnika na prvoj crti“. Knjiga ne sadrži novo pisanje, nego **propovijedi i govore koje je već održao**. Naslov, kaže, ne znači da se predstavlja kao *biskup na prvoj crti*. Odnosi se na biskupiju i područje, osobito ono **između Une i Kupe**, koje je u svim ratovima bilo područje velikih osvajanja i razaranja te velike patnje hrvatskoga katoličkog puka. U knjizi su, među ostalim, govori iz **Bleiburga** i iz **Ludbrega 2016.** te tumačenja **socijalnog nauka Crkve** o tome kako bi se katolici trebali odnositi prema politici. Opet naglašava da *nije favorizirao ni propagirao nijednu stranku*, kako su to neki htjeli prikazati, jer se može pročitati što je zapravo rekao.

Zbirku poezije, otkriva, *pabirčio je još od studentskih dana*. Kako ne bi bile samo pjesme, dodao je i nekoliko **crtica**. U jednoj od njih, nastaloj tijekom pohoda **ad limina**, zamislio je razgovor sa **svetim Petrom**: kako je Petar došao u **Rim**, središte carstva, a Isus nije. Ta ga je misao zanimala, pa ju je *malo problematizirao*. U zbirku je uvrstio i tridesetak **molitava** kojima je uglavnom završavao svoje propovijedi.

magisterium.assessment: U dostavljenom dijelu pretežno se govori o knjigama, propovijedima, poeziji i talentima biskupa; nema jasne teološke tvrdnje koja bi proturječila katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Budući da je tekst prekinut, a javna molitva krunice i ostale navedene teme nisu ovdje izložene dovoljno cjelovito, njihovu se usklađenost ne može pouzdano ocijeniti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk potvrđuje da kršćani trebaju javno svjedočiti vjeru, uz čistu savjest i bez dvosmislenosti. Krunica je pritom predstavljena kao molitva koja usredotočuje vjernika na Kristova otajstva te može biti vrijedna prilika za katehezu i evangelizaciju, osobito u zajedničkom slavlju.

sections.subtitle_en: From Parish Priest to Bishop on the Front Line: Homilies, Poetry, and a Conversation with Saint Peter
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host shows the book Bishop on the Front Line, and the guest explains how it came to be
sections.content_en:
The host recalls the rich written opus of Monsignor Košić. Along with the book **“Parish Priest on the Front Line”**, the sequel **“Bishop on the Front Line”** was also published, which the host shows in the studio. The bishop also wrote a **poetry collection**, and he also has a talent for singing. The host is interested to know if there is another talent that the public does not know about.

The bishop first clarifies the origin of the second book. “Bishop on the Front Line” was proposed to him by his collaborators after the release of “Parish Priest on the Front Line”. The book does not contain new writing, but **homilies and speeches that he had already delivered**. The title, he says, does not mean that he presents himself as a *bishop on the front line*. It refers to the diocese and the area, especially the one **between the Una and the Kupa**, which in all wars was an area of great conquests and destruction and great suffering of the Croatian Catholic people. In the book are, among others, speeches from **Bleiburg** and from **Ludbreg 2016**, as well as interpretations of the **social teaching of the Church** on how Catholics should relate to politics. He emphasizes again that he *did not favor or propagate any party*, as some wanted to portray, because one can read what he actually said.

The poetry collection, he reveals, *he had been gleaning ever since his student days*. So that they would not be just poems, he also added several **sketches**. In one of them, written during the **ad limina** visit, he imagined a conversation with **Saint Peter**: how Peter came to **Rome**, the center of the empire, and Jesus did not. That thought interested him, so he *problematized it a bit*. In the collection he also included about thirty **prayers** with which he mostly ended his homilies.

sections.subtitle: Deset godina u komisiji Justitia et Pax
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o iskustvu vođenja komisije HBK Justitia et Pax
sections.content:
Mons. Košić otkriva odakle dolaze njegovi stavovi o društvenim i političkim pitanjima. Do njih je, kaže, došao i zato što je **deset godina bio na čelu komisije HBK Justitia et Pax**.

To razdoblje opisuje s mnogo zahvalnosti. Imao je, kako kaže, **dobru ekipu stručnjaka i doktora znanosti** koji su razumjeli stvari. Mnogo je naučio od njih, a zajedno su se *borili za pravedne stvari*.

To iskustvo, zaključuje, oblikovalo ga je jednako kao i rat te kao područje biskupije u kojem djeluje i za koje je postavljen za pastira.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: opisuje formaciju za društvena pitanja i zauzimanje za pravednost, što odgovara crkvenom pozivu da se vjera očituje u zalaganju za pravdu i opće dobro. Budući da ne navodi konkretne stavove ni postupke komisije, nije moguće procijeniti njihovu sadržajnu ispravnost.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk društveni angažman ne smatra zamjenom za evangelizaciju, nego važnim dijelom svjedočenja koje promiče dostojanstvo osobe i pravedniji društveni poredak; crkveno je poslanje pritom oblikovati savjest i pridonositi raspravi, a ne preuzeti političku vlast. Biblijski temelj takvog zalaganja nalazi se u pozivu da se čine pravda i milosrđe te da se služi najmanjima, dok načela socijalnog nauka pomažu razlučiti kako pravednim ciljevima težiti primjerenim sredstvima.

sections.subtitle_en: Ten years in the Justitia et Pax commission
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about the experience of leading the HBK Justitia et Pax commission
sections.content_en:
Msgr. Košić reveals where his stances on social and political issues come from. He arrived at them, he says, also because **for ten years he was at the head of the HBK Justitia et Pax commission**.

He describes that period with much gratitude. He had, as he says, **a good team of experts and doctors of science** who understood things. He learned a lot from them, and together they *fought for just causes*.

That experience, he concludes, shaped him just as much as the war and the area of the diocese in which he ministered and for which he was appointed as shepherd.

sections.subtitle: Gitara, utakmice i krunica uz Kupu
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup Košić s osmijehom priča o šetnjama uz Kupu s krunicom u ruci
sections.content:
Na pitanje o talentima biskup spominje **glazbu**. Pjeva sada uglavnom na svetim misama, u liturgiji. Gitaru još ponekad uzme, ali sve rjeđe. Nekad je znao zapjevati u društvu ili u opuštenoj atmosferi, no za to sada, priznaje, nema mnogo vremena.

Volio je i **sport, nogomet i košarku**, ali danas uglavnom samo gleda utakmice. S osmijehom dodaje da *nije ni u dobi* u kojoj bi se mogao aktivno baviti sportom.

Najviše od svega voli **šetnje**, i to često **uz Kupu**. Tijekom tih šetnji moli **krunicu**. Ali molitvu često prekine netko tko ga pozdravi i pita kako je. *Sada ga već svi u Sisku poznaju*, kaže, iako ga prije nisu prepoznavali. Zato je znao birati stranu na kojoj nema mnogo ljudi: ne prema centru, nego dolje prema mostu. To ga veseli, kaže, i to bi volio nastaviti, *ako Bog da i dok Bog da*.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opisuje glazbu, sport i šetnje kao osobne interese te ne iznosi tvrdnju koja bi bila protivna katoličkom nauku. Katolička tradicija prihvaća takvu rekreaciju kao primjerenu, uz razboritu mjeru i bez zanemarivanja duhovnih i životnih dužnosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Sveti Franjo Saleški navodi šetnju, glazbu i sport među dopuštenim oblicima odmora, ali upozorava da ne smiju zauzeti previše vremena ni postati pretjerana zaokupljenost. Crkva također vidi odgojnu vrijednost sporta te naglašava da rekreacija treba biti usklađena s duhovnim životom i sudjelovanjem u nedjeljnoj liturgiji.

sections.subtitle_en: Guitar, matches, and the Rosary along the Kupa
sections.screenshot_description_en: Bishop Košić speaks with a smile about walks along the Kupa with a Rosary in hand
sections.content_en:
To the question about talents, the bishop mentions **music**. He now sings mostly at Holy Masses, in the liturgy. He still takes up the guitar sometimes, but ever more rarely. He used to sing in company or in a relaxed atmosphere, but for that now, he admits, he does not have much time.

He also loved **sports, soccer, and basketball**, but today mostly only watches matches. With a smile he adds that *he is not even at the age* when he could actively engage in sports.

Most of all he loves **walks**, and often **along the Kupa**. During these walks he prays the **Rosary**. But the prayer is often interrupted by someone who greets him and asks how he is. *Now everyone in Sisak already knows him*, he says, although earlier they did not recognize him. That is why he used to choose the side where there are not many people: not toward the center, but down toward the bridge. That brings him joy, he says, and he would like to continue that, *if God wills and as long as God wills*.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: Sisak ili Zagreb?
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup odgovara na blic pitanje Sisak ili Zagreb
sections.content:
Pred kraj razgovora voditelj najavljuje **blic pitanja** po načelu „ili-ili“. Ispričava se što ih nije unaprijed najavio i napominje da će neka biti *možda malo provokativna, ali ne i zlonamjerna*. Biskup se našali da *ne mora odgovoriti*, a voditelj odgovara da će se već dogovoriti.

Prvo pitanje glasi: **Sisak ili Zagreb?** Biskup odgovara diplomatski i temeljito. Zagreb je glavni grad Hrvatske i metropola koju ne može odbaciti jer je u njoj služio. Kada je došao u Sisak, imao je pedeset godina, a od toga je **više od 25 provelo u Zagrebu**. Nabraja i ostale postaje: rodni varaždinski kraj, vojsku, Karlovac, župničku službu u **Hrastovici** i **Petrinji**. Zatim navodi zagrebačke godine: školovanje, kapelaniju u **Španskom**, fakultet i službu pomoćnog biskupa. Zbrojeno, više je godina proveo u Zagrebu nego izvan njega.

Ipak, presuda je jasna: **„Sad sam u Sisku i to mi je najdraži grad.“** Voditelj dodaje da se ne mora odreći Zagreba, a biskup napominje da je to trebalo malo protumačiti gledateljima, *da se ne uvrijede ljudi iz Zagreba*.

magisterium.assessment: U opisanom dijelu nema izričitih tvrdnji o vjeri ili moralu koje bi se mogle ocijeniti kao protivne katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Odgovor o Sisku i Zagrebu prikazan je kao osobno i diplomatsko razmišljanje, a ne kao teološka tvrdnja.
magisterium.enrichment: Osobna privrženost različitim gradovima i zahvalnost za životna iskustva sama po sebi ne predstavljaju teološki problem. Budući da je odlomak prekinut usred rečenice, procjena se odnosi samo na dostavljeni sažetak i ne može obuhvatiti ostatak biskupova odgovora.
magisterium.assessment_en: In the described part, there are no explicit claims about faith or morals that could be assessed as contrary to Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. The answer about Sisak and Zagreb is presented as a personal and diplomatic reflection, not as a theological claim.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Personal attachment to different cities and gratitude for life experiences in themselves do not present a theological problem. Since the passage is interrupted mid-sentence, the assessment relates only to the provided summary and cannot encompass the rest of the bishop's response.

sections.subtitle_en: Rapid-fire questions: Sisak or Zagreb?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop answers the rapid-fire question Sisak or Zagreb
sections.content_en:
Towards the end of the conversation, the host announces **rapid-fire questions** on the principle of "either-or". He apologizes for not announcing them in advance and notes that some will be *perhaps a little provocative, but not malicious*. The bishop jokes that *he does not have to answer*, and the host replies that they will come to an agreement.

The first question is: **Sisak or Zagreb?** The bishop answers diplomatically and thoroughly. Zagreb is the capital of Croatia and a metropolis he cannot dismiss because he served in it. When he arrived in Sisak, he was fifty years old, and of that, he spent **more than 25 in Zagreb**. He also lists the other stations: his native Varaždin region, the military, Karlovac, parish ministry in **Hrastovica** and **Petrinja**. Then he mentions the Zagreb years: schooling, chaplaincy in **Špansko**, university, and service as an auxiliary bishop. In total, he spent more years in Zagreb than outside of it.

Nevertheless, the verdict is clear: **"Now I am in Sisak and that is my favorite city."** The host adds that he does not have to renounce Zagreb, and the bishop notes that this needed to be explained a little to the viewers, *so that the people from Zagreb do not get offended*.

sections.subtitle: Propovijed ili razgovor, crkva ili čovjek
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Košić naglašava da je obnova čovjeka važnija od obnove crkava
sections.content:
Sljedeće pitanje glasi: **propovijed ili neformalni razgovor s vjernicima?** Biskup priznaje da je sada gotovo neprestano u prvoj ulozi, ali da mu je **draža neformalna komunikacija**. Tada može objasniti svoje stavove i vjeru te čuti pitanja, što je *ljepše nego samo odozgora*. Propovijed je ipak liturgijski čin u kojem nema mjesta dijalogu. Njegova je obveza **protumačiti riječ Božju**, primijeniti je na sadašnji trenutak i dati poruku.

Posljednje pitanje posebno je važno za biskupa koji upravo obnavlja desetke crkava nakon potresa: **obnova crkve ili obnova čovjeka?** Odgovor je nedvosmislen: **obnova čovjeka sigurno je važnija**, što je, kaže, rekao već više puta. Crkve se mogu obnoviti *u zlatu i srebru*, ali upozorava na dvije opasnosti:

- da **ljudi nestanu**, što se, nažalost, već dogodilo jer su mnogi nakon potresa otišli iz kraja,
- da **ljudi postanu ruševine**, što smatra najgorim i nečim što se ne bi smjelo dogoditi.

Zato se, kaže, svi bore pomoći svakom čovjeku koji je u problemima, koji se muči i *trga*. Zaključuje: **apsolutni je prioritet čovjek**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen: ispravno ističe da je homilija liturgijski čin utemeljen na Božjoj riječi te da propovjednik treba protumačiti riječ Božju i povezati je sa životom vjernika. Ipak, tvrdnju da u homiliji „nema mjesta dijalogu” valja razumjeti samo kao napomenu da homilija nije razgovor s izmjenom replika, jer je crkveni nauk opisuje kao dijalog Boga i njegova naroda.
concerns: Ako se „nema mjesta dijalogu” shvati kao da u homiliji nema nikakvog dijaloškog odnosa, to bi bilo neprecizno: liturgijska navještajna riječ dio je dijaloga Boga i njegova naroda, premda se ne odvija kao neformalna rasprava između propovjednika i slušatelja.
magisterium.enrichment: Homilija se razlikuje od neformalnog razgovora po svojem liturgijskom kontekstu i služenju naviještenoj riječi, a ne po tome što bi bila jednosmjerno obraćanje bez odgovora vjernika: slušatelji u vjeri primaju riječ i nastavljaju razgovor s Bogom. Zato propovjednik treba poznavati zajednicu i tumačiti biblijske tekstove tako da podupru susret s Kristom i kršćanski život, bez svođenja homilije na osobno mišljenje ili nepovezano izlaganje.

citations.document_author: Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned: it correctly emphasizes that the homily is a liturgical act founded on the word of God and that the preacher should interpret the word of God and connect it with the life of the faithful. However, the assertion that in the homily there is “no room for dialogue” should be understood only as a remark that the homily is not a conversation with an exchange of remarks, because Church teaching describes it as a dialogue between God and his people.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The homily differs from an informal conversation by its liturgical context and its service to the proclaimed word, not by being a one-way address without a response from the faithful: the listeners receive the word in faith and continue the conversation with God. Therefore, the preacher should know the community and interpret biblical texts in such a way that they support the encounter with Christ and Christian life, without reducing the homily to personal opinion or an unrelated exposition.
concerns_en: If “there is no room for dialogue” is understood as meaning that there is no dialogical relationship whatsoever in the homily, that would be inaccurate: the liturgical word of proclamation is part of the dialogue between God and his people, even though it does not take place as an informal discussion between the preacher and the listeners.

sections.subtitle_en: Sermon or conversation, church or man
sections.screenshot_description_en: Msgr. Košić emphasizes that the renewal of man is more important than the renewal of churches
sections.content_en:
The next question is: **a sermon or an informal conversation with the faithful?** The bishop admits that he is now almost constantly in the first role, but that **informal communication is dearer to him**. Then he can explain his views and faith and hear questions, which is *nicer than just from above*. A sermon is nonetheless a liturgical act in which there is no room for dialogue. His duty is to **interpret the word of God**, apply it to the present moment, and give a message.

The last question is especially important for a bishop who is currently rebuilding dozens of churches after the earthquake: **the renewal of the church or the renewal of man?** The answer is unequivocal: **the renewal of man is certainly more important**, which, he says, he has already stated several times. Churches can be rebuilt *in gold and silver*, but he warns of two dangers:

- that **people disappear**, which, unfortunately, has already happened because many left the region after the earthquake,
- that **people become ruins**, which he considers the worst and something that should not happen.

That is why, he says, everyone is struggling to help every person who is in trouble, who struggles and *tears themselves apart*. He concludes: **man is the absolute priority**.

sections.subtitle: Biskupov blagoslov za kraj i najava razgovora o evolucijskoj psihologiji
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Vlado Košić podjeljuje blagoslov studiju, udruzi i gledateljima
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje biskupu od srca na sudjelovanju i izražava uvjerenje da je *mnogima progovorio*. Za kraj ga moli za **blagoslov studija, udruge i svih gledatelja**. Mons. Košić blagoslov podjeljuje liturgijskim obrascem: „Gospodin s vama.“ Slijede zazivi „Budi ime Gospodnje blagoslovljeno“ i „Pomoć je naša u imenu Gospodina“, na koje voditelj odgovara. Biskup završava riječima: **„Blagoslovio vas i sve vaše svemogući Bog, Otac i Sin i Duh Sveti.“**

Voditelj se zatim odjavljuje i poziva gledatelje da lajkaju, dijele i pretplate se na kanal te da, koliko mogu, podupru rad podcasta. Najavljuje da je sljedeća epizoda **Redefinicije** već dostupna preko **Patreon** profila.

Za kraj slijedi kratki isječak iz sljedeće epizode. Sugovornica, **evolucijska biologinja**, govori o **evolucijskoj psihologiji**. Smatra je važnom, ali u tom području vidi *veliko neznanje*. Najviše ju je, kaže, šokiralo kada je proučila predmete na studiju psihologije: na njemu ima *jako malo biologije*.

magisterium.assessment: Opisani završni blagoslov uglavnom odgovara obrascu biskupskog blagoslova u Rimskom misalu: uključuje liturgijski pozdrav, zazive i završni blagoslov u ime Trojstva. U odlomku nema vidljivog sadržaja koji bi bio protivan katoličkom nauku.
magisterium.enrichment: Blagoslov zaziva Božju naklonost nad okupljenima, a njegovo izričito spominjanje Oca, Sina i Duha Svetoga naglašava da kršćanski blagoslov ima trojstveno središte. Misal predviđa sličan obrazac s odgovorima zajednice „Sada i uvijeke“ i „Koji stvori nebo i zemlju“, čime se blagoslov povezuje sa zajedničkom molitvom Crkve.
magisterium.assessment_en: The described final blessing largely corresponds to the formula of a bishop's blessing in the Roman Missal: it includes the liturgical greeting, invocations, and the final blessing in the name of the Trinity. There is no visible content in the passage that would be contrary to Catholic teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The blessing invokes God's favor upon those gathered, and its explicit mention of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit emphasizes that Christian blessing has a Trinitarian center. The Missal provides for a similar formula with the community's responses „Now and forever“ and „Who made heaven and earth“, thereby connecting the blessing to the communal prayer of the Church.

sections.subtitle_en: The bishop's blessing for the end and announcement of a conversation on evolutionary psychology
sections.screenshot_description_en: Msgr. Vlado Košić imparts a blessing to the studio, the association, and the viewers
sections.content_en:
The host thanks the bishop from the heart for participating and expresses the conviction that he *spoke to many*. For the end, he asks him for a **blessing of the studio, the association, and all viewers**. Msgr. Košić imparts the blessing with the liturgical formula: „The Lord be with you.“ There follow the invocations „Blessed be the name of the Lord“ and „Our help is in the name of the Lord“, to which the host responds. The bishop concludes with the words: **„May almighty God bless you and all of yours, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.“**

The host then signs off and invites the viewers to like, share, and subscribe to the channel and to support the work of the podcast as much as they can. He announces that the next episode of **Redefinicija** is already available via the **Patreon** profile.

At the end, a short clip from the next episode follows. The interlocutor, an **evolutionary biologist**, speaks about **evolutionary psychology**. She considers it important, but sees *great ignorance* in that field. What shocked her most, she says, was when she examined the subjects in the study of psychology: there is *very little biology* in it.
